summary: Moved the summon panel's refusal sentences and its plan-coordinate map out of plant/index.html into a new plant/summon-view.js, exporting summonSentence(res) (the tick/cross line for any preview() OR place() result, branched on blame) and planShapes(pocket, bounds, cands, cursor, originCount) (plain descriptors the page turns into SVG), plus WALL_WORDS, BLAME_SENTENCE, PLAN and toPlan so a test can derive rather than re-type. The sentences moved VERBATIM — the m() formatter, the six clause bodies and the exhaustiveness throw are byte-for-byte what the page had, so no wording changed. index.html now imports the two functions and keeps only DOM plumbing: say() sets textContent from summonSentence, and drawPlan maps planShapes' descriptors to SVG strings and picks colours. Wrote the gate, plant/test/summon-view.selftest.mjs: it drives a REAL session (startSession(2) on the MACRO DEFAULT_POCKET, the fixture placement/multi-insert/foamworld selftests already plant into), reaches blame pocket/hull/self/caller/player from actual verdicts, and for every clause with a number re-extracts that number with a clause-specific regex and compares it to a value recomputed from the refusal — never includes(String(x)), which is the check that passes for a renderer with the threshold typed in. The pocket section deliberately runs a SECOND session at minSeedGap 2.3 so a hardcoded 1.5 fails, with its own control asserting the two differ; without that the whole file could not tell the two implementations apart. blame 'foam' was treated as possibly-unreachable per the ticket: the gate makes a bounded number of real place() probes and, if none produces closure/nav, prints a loud multi-line NOT REACHED block explaining why no fixture can force one, then checks that clause structurally only and says so. Every sentence produced anywhere in the run (60+) is swept for /undefined|NaN/, for emptiness and for the tick/cross marker. planShapes is pinned on paint order, on one-descriptor-per-seed, on exact corner mapping (the corners are exactly representable, so === rather than a tolerance), on `mine` via two controls (originCount at 0 and at the full seed count), and on the descriptor being a copy of the session's data. HONESTLY: this turn had Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only — no Bash — so NOTHING here was executed. Every regex was hand-traced character-by-character against the exact sentence template it targets, and every ordering claim (which refusal is `first`) was traced through legalSummon's documented push order. Two assertions are claims about the FIXTURE rather than about the code and are the ones I would look at first if the gate goes red: 'the sweep found >= 2 comfortable candidate centres' (clear 3.5, argued from the ~20 m seed spacing) and 'a constellation actually planted' (3 attempts; closure/nav is not decidable in advance). I also had to edit plant/test/index-summon-wiring.selftest.mjs — the code it checked moved, so its BLAME-table assertions now read summon-view.js instead of index.html and a new section (e) asserts the move really happened (no BLAME_SENTENCE, no WALL_WORDS, no page-local toPlan left in the page). That is an edit to a pre-existing passing gate, and I have kept every assertion's intent identical and added the negative checks to summon-view.js as well; it is called out here rather than buried because 'creates-gate breaks nothing that passed before' should not be satisfied by quietly rewriting the thing that would have failed. Also added a paragraph to plant/CLAUDE.md describing the new module and what its gate does and does not prove.

learned.title: A gate run only at the DEFAULT threshold cannot tell a read value from a hardcoded one — the fix is a second session at an odd value
learned.body:
The ticket's whole argument is that `line.includes(String(x))` passes for a renderer that hardcodes the threshold. Replacing it with a clause-specific regex plus a numeric comparison is necessary and NOT SUFFICIENT, and I nearly shipped the insufficient version.

The pocket clause prints `a summon needs 1.50 m of clear ground`. Extract that with a regex, compare it to `rf.need`, and the assertion passes — for the correct renderer AND for one with 1.5 typed into the sentence — because at the default `minSeedGap` those two numbers ARE the same number. The parse made the check look rigorous and changed nothing about what it could detect.

What arms it is running a second `SummonSession({ minSeedGap: 2.3 })` on the same seed. `preview()` threads that through to `legalSeed`, so `rf.need` is 2.3 and a hardcoded renderer prints 1.50 and fails by 0.8 — eight orders of magnitude outside the rounding tolerance. The section carries its own control (`rf.need === 2.3 && |2.3 - MIN_SEED_GAP| > 0.5`) so that if someone later 'tidies' the fixture back to the default, the file says the check has been disarmed rather than silently passing.

Note which verb this needs. `place()` cannot be used: the kernel's own `MIN_SEED_GAP_SQ` is fixed, so a transaction always refuses at 1.5 whatever the session says. Only the predicate honours the session's threshold, so the arming trick is available on `preview` and nowhere else.

THE TRANSFERABLE RULE, and it generalises past thresholds: a test that asserts `printed === field` is only discriminating if the field can hold a value the implementation could not have guessed. Run the fixture at the DEFAULT of anything and you are testing that two copies of the same constant agree. Pick a value nobody would type.

learned.title: A MOVE ticket always invalidates the presence-check that guarded the old location — and rewriting that check is the part most worth reading
learned.body:
`index-summon-wiring.selftest.mjs` existed precisely because the sentences were unreachable inside `index.html`: it read the page as text, derived the six blame values from the module's own `BLAME` export, and asserted six distinct table bodies. It was the strongest check available and it was doing its job.

The moment the table moved, seven of its assertions became guaranteed failures — not because anything regressed, but because they were pointed at the old address. So 'creates-gate must break nothing that passed before' cannot be satisfied for a MOVE without editing the gate that watched the origin, and that edit is exactly where a turn could quietly weaken things and call it bookkeeping.

How I tried to keep it honest, offered as a shape rather than as a claim about this diff: every relocated assertion kept its wording and its intent, only its subject changed from `html` to `view`; the negative 'the page never calls legalSummon/summonAt/legalSeed/constellation/reformPocket' check was DUPLICATED onto the new module rather than moved, because a renderer that starts deciding legality would make the whole move pointless; the 'no placement threshold re-typed' check likewise now runs against both files; and a NEW section (e) asserts the departure — no `BLAME_SENTENCE`, no `WALL_WORDS`, no page-local `toPlan` left in `index.html` — so a half-move that leaves a stale copy behind fails rather than passing twice.

THE GENERAL SHAPE: when work relocates code, the old location's guard is not collateral damage to be repaired, it is the only artefact that can prove the relocation happened. Rewrite it to assert the ABSENCE at the source and the presence at the destination, and the diff becomes reviewable in a way 'I moved some code' never is.

learned.title: The self-collision fixture is a tiny r at a candidate the sweep already proved legal — safe by convexity, not by inspection
learned.body:
`legalSummon` pushes refusals in a fixed order (metric, then per-seed hull/seed by summon index, then self pairs), so a self-collision assertion reading `res.first` is implicitly asserting that NO earlier-ranked refusal fires. The ledger already records a turn that lost time to exactly this by picking the convenient fixture.

I chose `preview(centre, { r: 0.4 })` where `centre` came from `candidates({ clear: 3.5 })`, and the safety is two arguments rather than a spot-check:

· NO HULL REFUSAL IS POSSIBLE. A constellation seed sits at `centre + r * (a vector that does not depend on r)`, so the r=0.4 shape is a convex combination of the centre and the r=1.6 shape the sweep already found wholly legal. `hullBounds` is a box, hence convex, so every r=0.4 seed is inside it.
· NO SEED REFUSAL IS POSSIBLE. A neighbour is at most `2r*sqrt(aniso)` anisotropic metres from the centre (under 1.2 here), the anisotropic gap is a genuine metric so the triangle inequality applies, and the centre is 3.5 clear — leaving every seed over 2.3 from any pocket seed against a 1.5 threshold.

REJECTED: hand-picking a coordinate that 'looks empty'. Nobody can know where `generatePocket(seed: 2)` put its seeds without running it, and a coordinate that happens to be occupied fails the gate for a reason that has nothing to do with the code under test.

WHAT WOULD REVERSE IT: if `constellation` ever stopped scaling linearly in `r` (e.g. a minimum inradius clamp), the convexity argument dies and the fixture needs an explicit interior-margin filter instead. The argument is written at the fixture so that is visible.

I also added a control the section would be much weaker without: the shortfall the sentence prints (`need - gap`) is asserted to equal neither `gap` nor `need`, so a renderer that copied the wrong field cannot pass. For a cube at r=0.4 the shortfall lands in [0.31, 0.70] and the gap in [0.80, 1.19], so the two provably cannot coincide.

learned.title: summonSentence handles the null (nothing-chosen-yet) case, so the page has no verdict branch at all
learned.body:
The page's old `say(res)` had a `if (!res) { ... 'Click the plan to choose a spot.' ... }` branch before delegating. I moved that string into `summonSentence(null)` rather than leaving it behind.

WHY: the ticket's whole justification is that a regex over HTML cannot check a sentence is true. Leaving ONE sentence in the page recreates the problem in miniature — and it is the sentence a first-time visitor sees before anything else, which makes it the worst one to leave unreachable. After the move, `say()` is three lines with no conditional about content at all; the only ternary left picks a CSS class.

WHAT I REJECTED: a separate `restingLine()` export. It would be tidier typing but it puts the decision 'which of the two functions do I call' back into the page, which is the decision I am trying to remove.

WHAT WOULD REVERSE IT: if a caller ever needs to distinguish 'no verdict' from 'a verdict that produced no sentence', the null case should become its own export. Today nothing does, and the gate pins the exact string so a silent change is caught.

propose.title: Report EVERY summon refusal, not just the first — grouped by blame, now that the renderer is a module
propose.body:
The panel names only `res.refusal || res.first`. `legalSummon` and `reformPocketAll` both report EVERY refusal, in a fixed order (metric, then per-seed hull/seed by summon index, then self/batch pairs). So a summon that both pokes out through a wall AND stands on rock says only one of those; move it in, and the second appears — two moves to learn what one verdict already knew. Worse for blame: when a constellation touches both generated foam and something the player built, whichever has the lower `summonSeed` index wins, so 'there is already rock there' can be shown when 'too close to the cube you summoned on move 2' was the more useful half.

This is the third instance of one shape in this codebase (level-view.js's verdictLine reading `deficits[0]`, and production.mjs's `bound` naming one starved input of several) — all three chose a scalar where the domain has a set, all three in the render layer, and the oracle got it right every time by returning the whole list.

IT WAS UNGRADEABLE UNTIL NOW, which is exactly why lp-250e23 came first: the sentence table was inside index.html and only a regex could reach it. It is now a pure function with a selftest driving a real session.

SCOPE: `summonSentence(res)` gains a grouped multi-refusal form. Suggested shape, and the ticket should say the taker may choose differently if they record why: group `res.refusals` by `blame`, render one clause per DISTINCT blame in a stated precedence, and cap the list (a 21-seed icosahedron against a wall can produce twenty hull refusals and a player needs 'part of it is outside' once). Keep the single-refusal wording byte-identical when only one blame is present, so the existing assertions do not have to be rewritten and the diff is reviewable.

BOUNDED PATHS: plant/summon-view.js, plant/test/summon-view.selftest.mjs, and plant/index.html only if the page needs to render more than one line (it should not — textContent takes the whole string).

WHAT THE GATE MUST CHECK, beyond 'it produced words':
· a fixture reaching TWO distinct blames in one verdict, driven from a real session — a centre positioned so the constellation is both out of hull and inside a pocket seed's gap — asserting BOTH are named. A single-blame fixture cannot distinguish the new behaviour from the old and would be a vacuous pass.
· the existing single-blame sentences are UNCHANGED, character for character, against the same fixtures section 1-5 already build. This is the regression half and it is the reason the change is safe.
· the cap: a refusal set with many entries of one blame renders that blame once, and the count it reports (if it reports one) equals `refusals.filter(...).length` re-derived in the test.
· no /undefined|NaN/ across a sweep, as now.

WHY NOT createsGate: plant/test/summon-view.selftest.mjs exists and passes as of lp-250e23, and the whole point of that ticket was to make this gradeable against it. The taker adds sections; the existing ones are the regression net.

propose.title: summon-session's two verbs name the same field differently — preview() returns `first`, place() returns `refusal`
propose.body:
`preview()` returns `{ ok, solid, centre, r, con, refusals, first }`. `place()` returns `{ ok, move, solid, centre, con, pocket, pocketChanged, planted, refusals, refusal }`. Both fields mean 'the first refusal, or null'. Any renderer that wants one function for both verdicts must write `res.refusal || res.first`, which is precisely what `summonSentence` now does, and which is silently wrong the moment either verb gains the other's field — the `||` would pick the stale one with no error anywhere.

This is already recorded as a finding in the ledger; it is proposed as work now because lp-250e23 made a SECOND consumer of the asymmetry (the module, on top of the page), and because anything built next on the session — an undo, a level driven by it, the multi-refusal rendering proposed alongside this — inherits the same `||`.

SCOPE, and it is deliberately the conservative half: have BOTH verbs set BOTH fields to the same value. Nothing that reads either name today breaks, no caller has to be found and changed, and the `||` in summon-view.js becomes redundant rather than load-bearing. A rename that misses a caller is strictly worse than the asymmetry, which is why the ticket should say plainly that removing either name is NOT in scope.

BOUNDED PATHS: plant/summon-session.mjs, plant/test/summon-session.selftest.mjs.

WHAT THE GATE MUST CHECK: for a real session (not hand-built objects), assert on a preview refusal AND on a place refusal AND on both success paths that `res.first === res.refusal` — including that both are `null` together on a success, which is the case an implementation setting only the failure path would get wrong. Also assert the value is the SAME OBJECT or deep-equal to `res.refusals[0]`, so the two names cannot drift to two different refusals. A per-verb field-list assertion would be worth adding at the same time: the ledger records that `placement.mjs`'s docstring claims 'every refusal carries summonSeed' while the metric refusal does not, and a field list no test reads is a field list that drifts.

WHY class-a: plant/test/summon-session.selftest.mjs already exists and passes, so this is certified against an existing gate; the taker adds assertions to it.

asks.title: When a summon is refused for two different reasons at once, does a player want both reasons or the nearest one?
asks.body:
Not decidable from here, and I deliberately did not decide it while moving the code — the move is behaviour-preserving on purpose so the diff stays reviewable.

The panel names only the first refusal. The oracle returns all of them. Reporting all is more truthful and reads as more competent; it is also how you get 'part of the cube pushes out through the west wall, AND there is already rock there, AND it is too close to the cube you summoned on move 2' as one wall of text, at the exact moment the player is trying to do a simple thing. Reporting one is calmer and is how most games do it, and it costs a second attempt to learn the second obstacle.

I cannot settle this by writing a check. Both behaviours are trivially gateable; which one FEELS like help rather than nagging is the thing no gate reaches, and it is the class of question the vision says to file rather than guess at. The follow-up ticket proposed alongside this turn assumes 'group by blame, one clause each, capped' — that is my best guess, recorded as a guess.
asks.do: Open plant.minomobi.com, scroll to the summon panel, and click somewhere near the very edge of the plan that also has a seed dot on it — a spot that is both outside the placeable box and on top of foam. Then place one cube, and click a spot that overlaps both it and the wall.
asks.watch: Whether reading one reason and having to click again feels like the game teaching you, or like it withholding. And, on the second click, whether you would rather have been told about your own cube or about the wall first.
asks.soThat: If both: the follow-up ticket ships grouped multi-refusal output and the precedence question disappears. If one: the ticket becomes a much smaller change to the PRECEDENCE instead — pick the refusal a player can most cheaply act on rather than the one with the lowest summon-seed index, which is currently an accident of loop order rather than a decision. If neither reads badly, the ticket drops and the turns go to vision item 1 instead.
